_comment: Gold canonical K-IR propositions for Benchmark v0. Each is the target equivalence class that paraphrase 'variants' (variants.json) should collapse onto. 'context' fields are the conditions/assumptions that make the statement true -- they are the whole point of the benchmark.

propositions.nl_gloss: Voltage equals current times resistance (Ohm's law).
propositions.notes: Classic law-of-nature proposition; no differentiability subtleties.

propositions.nl_gloss: For metals, electrical resistance increases as temperature increases.

context.domain: normal_operating_range (no phase change, no superconducting transition)

propositions.notes: dR/dT > 0 for metals. Deliberately paired with K003 to test context-sensitive contradiction handling.

propositions.nl_gloss: For semiconductors, electrical resistance decreases as temperature increases.
propositions.notes: dR/dT < 0 for semiconductors. Surface-level negation of K002; correct system must NOT mark K002/K003 as CONTRADICTS once material_class context is taken into account -- they are UNRELATED (different subject material), not contradictory.

propositions.nl_gloss: A solid body's linear dimensions increase as its temperature increases, at constant pressure.
propositions.notes: General thermal expansion law for solids.

propositions.nl_gloss: Metals expand when heated.
propositions.notes: SPECIALIZATION of K004 (metal is instance_of Material/solid). Correct relation to K004: K004m ENTAILS-nothing-new / K004 ENTAILS K004m is the wrong direction -- actually K004 (general) ENTAILS K004m (specific) given Metal instance_of solid-forming material. Used to test the 'specialization mistaken for identity' failure mode.

propositions.nl_gloss: Copper expands when heated.
propositions.notes: SPECIALIZATION of K004m (Copper instance_of Metal). K004m ENTAILS K004c, not EQUAL. This is the canonical 'false merge' trap case from the design discussion.

propositions.nl_gloss: Density equals mass divided by volume.
propositions.notes: Definitional identity, always true, no context needed.

propositions.nl_gloss: Ideal gas law: PV = nRT.
propositions.notes: Fails for real gases at high pressure / low temperature -- context is load-bearing.

propositions.nl_gloss: Newton's second law: F = ma.
propositions.notes: Classic law; context excludes relativistic speeds and variable-mass systems (e.g. rockets).

propositions.statement: Boiling(x) <=> (Temperature(x) >= BoilingPoint(x, Pressure(x)) AND PhaseState(x) = liquid)
propositions.nl_gloss: A liquid boils when its temperature reaches the boiling point at the current pressure.
propositions.notes: Rule with an explicit conjunctive condition; used to test hyperedge/AND handling.

propositions.nl_gloss: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at 1 atmosphere of pressure.
propositions.notes: Instance fact, not a general law. Boiling point changes with pressure/altitude -- context is load-bearing.

propositions.nl_gloss: Electrical power equals current times voltage.
propositions.notes: Definitional; combines with K001 to derive K011 (tests substitution-based ENTAILS, not surface EQUAL).

propositions.nl_gloss: Electrical power dissipated equals current squared times resistance.
propositions.notes: Derivable from K001 + K010 by substitution (V=IR into P=IV). Relation to K001/K010: ENTAILED_BY {K001, K010} jointly (hyperedge), not EQUAL to either alone.

propositions.nl_gloss: Average velocity equals distance divided by time.
propositions.notes: Fails for non-uniform motion without qualifying as 'average'.

propositions.nl_gloss: Heat added equals mass times specific heat times temperature change.
propositions.notes: Breaks down during phase transitions (latent heat dominates instead).

propositions.nl_gloss: For a fixed mass, escape velocity increases as radius decreases.
propositions.notes: escape_velocity ~ sqrt(mass/radius); monotonicity only holds at fixed mass.

propositions.nl_gloss: Water expands when heated.
propositions.notes: TRUE only above 4C. See K016 for the anomalous region -- deliberately constructed contradiction-via-omitted-context pair.

propositions.nl_gloss: Water contracts as it is heated between 0C and 4C (anomalous expansion).
propositions.notes: Surface form looks like it CONTRADICTS K015. Correct classification once temperature_domain context is included: neither CONTRADICTS nor UNRELATED -- both are true, in disjoint context windows (OVERLAPS-by-subject, but truth-conditionally compatible once context is resolved). This is the single most important test case in v0.

propositions.nl_gloss: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge.
propositions.notes: Definitional identity.

propositions.nl_gloss: Metals are conductors.
propositions.notes: Ontological fact, not a causal/quantitative law -- tests that the classifier doesn't force everything into MONOTONIC_* form.

propositions.nl_gloss: No material is both a metal and a semiconductor.
propositions.notes: Supports resolving K002/K003 as UNRELATED rather than CONTRADICTS, since their subjects are disjoint types.

propositions.statement: Volume(x) is CONSERVED under uniform_scaling(x) iff shape unchanged
propositions.nl_gloss: Scaling an object uniformly changes its volume unless the shape is held exactly proportional in a way that keeps volume fixed (trivial/never in practice).
propositions.notes: Deliberately awkward/edge-case proposition to stress-test the classifier on a near-vacuous statement; expect low agreement -- included for calibration, not as a load-bearing fact.
